label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common) while the policy strongly favors a2, early-to-mid episode
explanation: This unit is active only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 (a common transition). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1, or after a rare a2->S1. Every D2 a2->S2c step gives recall 1.0 but precision 0.38 (F1 0.56). The policy readout separates the two: the unit fires when choice (logit a1 - a2) < -4.44, i.e. the agent strongly prefers repeating a2, which brings F1 to 0.81. It also turns off late in the episode: almost nothing after trial ~70, nothing at trials 90-99. Adding ep_trial < 75 gives dev P 0.87 / R 0.95 / F1 0.91 / mass recall 0.98. All variables are observed or computed by the model, so no future variables are used. On magnitude: high value-head output (>8.1) covers 81% of top-quartile activations but only 24% of the bottom quartile, so a larger expected value means a larger activation. In the examples, magnitude also tends to be highest on the first a2->S2c after a rare or unrewarded trial and to decay slowly over runs of repeated a2->S2c (not quantified). It is S2/a2-specific: good = S1 carries only 2% of the mass. The ep_trial cutoff is an empirical dependence on episode time and probably reflects slow hidden-state drift.

issues: The structural claims hold on the test split. The unit has zero activations at D1 and GO, after a1, after rare a2->S1, and at in_rew==1. The base predicate D2 & a2 & S2 gives recall 1.000 with precision 0.36. Adding choice < -4.44 gives F1 0.813, and adding ep_trial < 75 gives the reported F1 0.903 and mass recall 0.98.

The episode-time effect is a gradual decline, not a sharp cutoff. Inside the choice-filtered D2 a2->S2c set, precision is 0.94 for trials 0-24, 0.92 for 25-49, 0.88 for 50-64, 0.55 for 65-74 and 0.015 for 75 and later. With ep_trial < 70 the test F1 is 0.913, only marginally better than the reported 0.903. The '<75' cutoff is a rough boundary, and many of the remaining false positives sit in trials 65-74.

The magnitude claims are weakly supported. Within the predicate, value > 8.1 raises precision to 0.92 and mass recall (0.69) exceeds recall (0.57), so magnitude does rise with value, as claimed. The claim that the 'first a2->S2c after a rare or unrewarded trial' is strongest is barely supported: the prev_reward==0 subset has mass share 0.23 against count share 0.21. It is untested and should be read as anecdotal.

I checked the misses on the test split and found nothing systematic. Missed activations hold 2.0% of the mass and are low-magnitude, scattered a2->S2c steps that fail the choice cutoff. The false positives are mostly late-episode steps (65-75) and steps right after a reversal to good=S1. The good=S1 subset of the predicate has precision 0.58 but covers only 3.7k steps.
